era: PlayStation 2 / Xbox / Nintendo handhelds / HD consoles
summary: EA Sports BIG's arcade snowboarding series; use PS2/PCSX2 for the original, Xbox/Xbox backward compatibility where it materially improves fidelity, and secondary GameCube only where Nintendo-exclusive content exists.

emulation.notes: Upscale the PS2 release for modern displays.

primary.why: The original SSX was a PlayStation 2 launch title and the only sourced release platform; PCSX2 can raise the fidelity ceiling while preserving the original content.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PS2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscaling.

emulation.notes: Use Xemu for the Xbox route; PS2/GameCube emulation is valid for preference checks.

primary.why: Tricky shipped on PS2, GameCube, Xbox, and GBA; the Xbox version is the chosen fidelity route for the home-console core game, while GBA is a downgraded handheld conversion.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or Xemu; use PS2/GameCube only for controller preference and GBA only for handheld curiosity.

entries.title: SSX 3

emulation.notes: Use Xbox One X/Series hardware for the enhanced route.

primary.why: SSX 3 shipped on sixth-generation consoles and handhelds, then the original Xbox version became backward compatible in 2018 and Xbox One X enhanced with 4K/60 support, making modern Xbox the strongest fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the backward-compatible Xbox version on Xbox One X or Xbox Series hardware; use original console/emulator routes only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Backward-compatible enhancement, not a remake; PS2 online multiplayer has been discontinued.

entries.title: SSX Out of Bounds
entries.definitive_edition: N-Gage original for this handheld offshoot

emulation.notes: Hardware/software preservation is the main route.

primary.why: Out of Bounds is a downsized handheld port of SSX 3 released for N-Gage, Gizmondo, and Symbian; the original N-Gage release is the clearest sourced preservation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on preserved N-Gage hardware/software if available; treat Gizmondo and Symbian as alternate handheld preservation routes.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not treat Out of Bounds as a replacement for SSX 3; it is a separate downsized handheld port.

entries.title: SSX on Tour
entries.definitive_edition: Xbox main route plus GameCube Nintendo-content secondary

emulation.emulator: Xemu primary; Dolphin for GameCube secondary
emulation.notes: Use Xemu for the Xbox route and Dolphin for the Nintendo-exclusive cleanup.

primary.why: The main console game shipped on Xbox, PS2, and GameCube, with PSP as a distinct reduced/borrowed-content version; Xbox is the fidelity route, while GameCube has Nintendo-exclusive characters/content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version for the main run, then play the GameCube version briefly for Mario, Luigi, Peach, and the Nintendo Village variant.

secondary.exclusive_content: Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, and the Nintendo Village version of Last Call with Mario-themed iconography.
secondary.what_to_play: Play or sample the GameCube version's Nintendo-exclusive characters and Nintendo Village course variant.
secondary.why: The Xbox version is the fidelity route, but the GameCube version has exclusive Nintendo crossover content.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster documented; PSP is a distinct reduced handheld version.

entries.title: SSX Blur

emulation.notes: Use real Wii controls where possible.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High-resolution Wii emulation with original controls

primary.why: Blur is a Wii-only entry built around Wii Remote and Nunchuk controls, adding slalom and motion-drawn Ubertricks while recycling/reworking earlier SSX content.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Wii hardware for the intended controls, or Dolphin with Wii Remote support if you want higher output resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster documented; much content is reworked from earlier games but the controls are unique to Wii.

entries.title: SSX

emulation.notes: Use Xbox One/Series hardware for the compatibility route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Backward-compatible Xbox 360 release on modern Xbox hardware

primary.version: Backward-compatible Xbox 360 release with DLC if preserved
primary.why: The reboot shipped on PS3, Xbox 360, and Android; the Xbox 360 version became Xbox One/Series backward compatible, and the DLC/update path adds Mount Eddie, classic characters, Mt. Fugi & Friends, Freeride, and 3-2-1 GO! modes when preserved.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 version through Xbox One/Series backward compatibility with owned DLC/updates installed; use PS3 only if your DLC ownership is there.

entries.remaster_caveats: Backward-compatible route, not a remaster; Android is not a substitute for the console release.
